about: The evangelium of the formulary “Quinquagesima Sunday” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: At that time, Jesus took aside the Twelve and said to them: Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and all that has been written by the prophets concerning the Son of Man will be accomplished. For He will be delivered to the Gentiles, mocked, scourged and spat upon; and after they have scourged Him, they will kill Him, and on the third day He will rise again. And they understood none of these things; this saying was hidden from them, and they did not understand what was being said. And it happened, as He drew near to Jericho, that a certain blind man was sitting by the wayside, begging. Hearing the crowd pass by, he asked what this meant. And they told him that Jesus of Nazareth was passing by. And he cried out, saying: Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me. And those who went ahead rebuked him so that he would be silent. But he cried out much more: Son of David, have mercy on me. And Jesus stood still and commanded that he be brought to Him. And when he had come near, He asked him, saying: What do you want Me to do for you? But he said: Lord, let me receive my sight. And Jesus said to him: Receive your sight; your faith has made you well. And immediately he saw and followed Him, glorifying God. And all the people, when they saw it, gave praise to God.

a.g: they understood none of these things
And Jesus stood still and commanded
do you want Me to do for you

ex.w035: The scourging precedes the announced killing. Flagellaverint can be future perfect indicative or perfect subjunctive. Postquam and the future occident support the former analysis here, although both moods share this form.
